purpose: How a merchant-processing / POS agent selects and vets ISO and agent programs, chooses and wins local merchant verticals, sells the POS-anchored bundle as one accountable relationship, runs honest statement-analysis diagnostics, and keeps every sales claim compliant so each signed merchant enters the book on disclosed, verifiable terms.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the operator is an independent local agent or small agency selling under one or more ISO/agent programs, not a registered processor or a bank
target merchants are card-present local SMBs (restaurants and food service, salons and personal care, convenience stores, auto repair) inside one trade area
all economics (interchange, assessments, markup, splits, hardware margin) are described as mechanisms with per-deal verification paths, never as asserted figures

compliance obligations (card-network rules, PCI-DSS, surcharging and cash-discount law, advertising rules) vary by jurisdiction, network and program, and current rules must be verified before any claim is used
exclusions: POS hardware/software matching, the application/underwriting/KYC path, installation, menu and catalog build, staff training, PCI scoping at deployment, and go-live support - the deployment-and-onboarding sibling KB's territory; this KB ends at the sold-deal handoff package

residual computation and payment mechanics, attrition management, support economics, chargeback education, cross-sell from the installed trusted-operator position, and portfolio valuation or sale - the residual-book sibling KB's territory

deceptive rate comparisons and guaranteed-savings claims of the form 'we will definitely save you X percent' - statement analysis is a diagnostic mechanism and savings are verified per merchant after conversion
stating interchange rates, markup levels, or residual split percentages as factual numbers - they appear only as mechanisms or qualitative bands verified per program and per deal
asserting card-network rule text, PCI-DSS obligations, or surcharging law specifics - these are compliance classes to flag, jurisdiction- and network-specific, to be verified currently before use
financial or legal advice to merchants or agents, and merchant underwriting decisions, which belong to the processor

competency_questions.question: Which route to market - sub-agent under an ISO, registered ISO, referral partner, or payfac reseller - fits a local bundle-led operator, and what does each route actually govern?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ISO_PROGRAM_LANDSCAPE distinguishes the routes by what each governs (merchant-relationship ownership, registration and selling identity, liability, economics mechanism, control), ACQUISITION_THESIS supplies the book-first selection criteria, and PROCESSOR_FIT_SELECTION turns the choice into a signed program

competency_questions.question: Which clauses of an agent agreement decide whether the agent ever owns the residual book, and how are they vetted before signing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AGENT_AGREEMENT_DILIGENCE names the deciding clause classes (residual survivability, portability and assignment, non-solicit, minimum-production, liability, termination events) and the extraction discipline that reads them from the signed text rather than the recruiter's pitch

competency_questions.question: How do interchange, network assessments, processor markup and the agent's share come to exist as layers, and how is the agent's own economics verified on a specific deal without asserting invented numbers?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ECONOMICS_MECHANISM_LITERACY attributes each layer to who sets it, what moves it, where it appears on a statement, and gives the Schedule-A-plus-residual-report verification path for the agent's own share

competency_questions.question: How does an agent choose one or two beachhead verticals and defend the choice with explicit criteria rather than a mood?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VERTICAL_SELECTION lists the scoring criteria (acceptance intensity, POS pain, decision-maker access, trade-area density, saturation, referral connectivity, underwriting acceptability) and labels the scores heuristic priors revisable by pipeline evidence

competency_questions.question: What does each target vertical concretely struggle with at the counter, and how does each pain map to a bundle element the agent can actually deliver and support?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VERTICAL_PAIN_PROFILING gives per-vertical operating pains in the merchant's own language, BUNDLE_ARCHITECTURE maps pains to bundle elements with the serviceability rule, and PROPOSAL_CONSTRUCTION carries the mapping into the merchant-facing document

competency_questions.question: How is the trade area turned into a named-account map with observable stack facts and trigger events that open deals?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOCAL_MARKET_MAPPING describes enumeration per vertical, the observable facts recorded per account, and the trigger events (openings, ownership changes, visible cost pain) that sequence visits

competency_questions.question: Which prospecting channels fit a trust-based local displacement sale, in what order, and why does cold volume underperform in this trade?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRUST_CHANNEL_PROSPECTING ranks walk-ins, merchant referrals, bookkeeper/supplier multipliers, association presence and outbound calling, with the borrowed-or-earned-trust logic for why displacement needs them

competency_questions.question: How is a merchant's processing statement analyzed honestly - pricing model, effective rate, fee drivers - and what may and may not be concluded from the diagnostic?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISCOVERY_AUDIT collects full multi-month statements and STATEMENT_ANALYSIS_METHOD identifies the pricing model, computes the effective rate from the merchant's own numbers, itemizes drivers, and separates structurally changeable from unchangeable components without any savings promise

competency_questions.question: Which sales-claim classes are compliance-sensitive - savings figures, surcharge and cash-discount programs, PCI statements, network marks and selling identity - and what form keeps each compliant?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SALES_CLAIM_COMPLIANCE maintains the claims register with approved forms and verify-current-rules flags per class, and SAVINGS_CLAIM_DISCIPLINE supplies the conditional-estimate-plus-verification form that replaces guaranteed-savings talk

competency_questions.question: What must be disclosed before any merchant signs, and how are vulnerable owners protected from pressure the sale could otherwise apply?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISCLOSURE_FIRST_SELLING lists the pre-signature disclosure set (term, exit mechanics, lease totals, processor identity, underwriting non-guarantee, provider map) and the vulnerable-owner slow-down protocol, and CLOSE_AND_EXPECTATION_SETTING enforces the checklist at signature

competency_questions.question: How is an incumbent processor or POS displaced ethically when contracts, leases and switching costs are in force, and how does the agent position against each competitor class?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INCUMBENT_DISPLACEMENT derives switching costs from the merchant's own confirmed documents and frames the decision as the merchant's conditional arithmetic, and COMPETITIVE_POSITIONING gives the honest wedge against telesales ISOs, banks, self-serve stacks and rival agents

competency_questions.question: Which merchants does the agent decline or refer elsewhere even when they are ready to sign, and why does that screen protect the book and the program relationship?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MERCHANT_RISK_FIT_SCREEN gives the category, red-flag, expectation and service-fit checks, the sign/decline/refer outcomes, and the boundary that underwriting remains the processor's decision

competency_questions.question: What does a complete sold-deal handoff to deployment contain, and where exactly does acquisition's responsibility end?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEPLOYMENT_HANDOFF_PACKAGE enumerates the package contents (application data, bundle scope, promises recap, statement baseline, pain profile and site facts, flagged risks) and states the boundary into the deployment sibling KB

competency_questions.question: How is acquisition run as a measured pipeline, and how do its readings feed back into vertical, channel and bundle decisions?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PIPELINE_CADENCE_METRICS defines the stages, the cadence over the account map, and the stage-conversion and channel readings - labeled heuristic priors until deals accumulate - that feed the revision loops

glossary.definition: A sales organization registered with the card networks through a sponsoring bank or processor to market payment acceptance; independent agents commonly sell as sub-agents under an ISO's registration rather than registering themselves, and which name they may sell under is governed by the program agreement and network rules.

The contract package under which an independent agent sells for an ISO or processor; Schedule A is its economics exhibit defining buy rates, revenue-share mechanics and bonus terms - the only authoritative statement of the agent's economics, superseding anything a recruiter said.

The fee component set by the card networks and paid to the card-issuing bank, varying by card product, merchant category and entry mode; no processor or agent sets it, and it moves only when the network tables or the merchant's acceptance mix move.

The structures a processor uses to charge a merchant: pass-through interchange plus a stated markup; qualified/mid/non-qualified buckets into which transactions are tiered; or one blended rate regardless of card mix. Identifying which model is in force is the first step of statement analysis.

The recurring share of processing economics paid to an agent under the program agreement; its size, conditions and survivability are governed entirely by the signed agreement, and its computation and payment mechanics belong to the portfolio-management sibling KB.

Total processing fees divided by total processed volume for a statement period - a descriptive diagnostic ratio computed from a specific merchant's own statement, not a price anyone quotes; it summarizes the combined effect of pricing model, card mix and fees.

The diagnostic reading of a merchant's processing statements to identify the pricing model in force, compute the effective rate, and itemize fee drivers; it produces a merchant-specific diagnostic, never a savings guarantee.

Two program classes for shifting card-acceptance cost toward card-paying customers; both are governed by card-network rules and state or provincial law, differ by jurisdiction, and are compliance classes to verify currently - never to assert from memory.

A contractual charge for ending a processing agreement before its term; in displacement it is read from the merchant's own contract and confirmed by the merchant, never guessed at or waved away by the soliciting agent.

The artifact that ends acquisition: application data as submitted, the sold bundle scope, the written promises recap, the statement baseline, the vertical pain profile and site facts, packaged so onboarding can execute without re-discovering the merchant.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for merchant_acquisition_and_vertical_targeting work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Fix what merchant acquisition exists to produce: a durable book of merchants whose processing economics and bundled services recur, not a stream of one-time POS hardware sales. Every acquisition choice - which program to sign under, which verticals to chase, what to promise at the table - is judged by what it does to the book: a merchant won on honest terms who stays for years outweighs a fatter one-time hardware commission, and a merchant likely to churn, chargeback, or feel deceived is a liability even when the deal closes cleanly. The thesis also fixes the positioning: a local trusted operator selling one accountable relationship (POS, card acceptance, phones, internet, cameras, support) rather than an anonymous rate peddler, because the relationship is what an incumbent cannot easily displace back.

excluded: residual computation and portfolio valuation (sibling KB)
deployment execution (sibling KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: retention and referral outcomes show whether the positioning is producing a durable book or a churn pool

pros.claim: A book-first frame rejects economically corrosive deals a commission-first frame accepts
pros.example: declining a lease-heavy quick close with a visibly reluctant restaurant owner because churn-and-resentment risk outweighs the upfront hardware margin

cons.claim: Book-first discipline sacrifices near-term cash an agent may genuinely need during the ramp years
cons.example: passing on easy one-time equipment flips while the residual base is still too small to cover rent

failure_modes: chasing upfront hardware commissions until the so-called book is a churn pool
positioning as a rate discounter and attracting only price shoppers who leave for the next discounter
acceptance_tests: a written acquisition charter states the book-of-merchants asset logic, the bundle-relationship positioning, and the ethical-selling commitments
revisit_triggers: the agent's cash position forces a mix shift toward upfront margin
a program change alters what recurs versus what pays once

nodes.definition: Map the routes to market an independent seller of merchant processing can take and what each actually is: a sub-agent selling under another ISO's registration; a registered ISO with its own sponsor-bank relationship, network registration duties and branding rights; a referral partner handing leads to a processor or POS ISV for a fee; and a reseller under a payment-facilitator model where merchants become sub-merchants of the payfac. Each route governs different things - who contractually owns the merchant relationship, who is registered to sell in whose name, who bears loss liability, how economics are shared as mechanisms (buy-rate spread, revenue share, per-referral fee), and how much control the seller keeps over pricing, POS choice and support. Choosing a route is choosing what kind of business the book will be, so the map is read against the acquisition thesis before any recruiter's pitch is entertained.

included: route taxonomy (sub-agent, registered ISO, referral partner, payfac reseller)
route choice against the book-first thesis
excluded: clause-level agreement reading
specific program economics figures

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new route structure (e.g. an ISV hybrid) appears in recruiting pitches or an existing route's governing terms shift industry-wide

pros.claim: Knowing what each route governs prevents signing into a structure that contradicts the book-first thesis
pros.example: spotting that a payfac reseller pitch leaves the merchant relationship owned by the payfac before falling for its easy boarding

cons.claim: The landscape blurs at the edges, so a clean taxonomy can misclassify hybrid offers
cons.example: a POS ISV 'partnership' marketed like an agent program that is really lead referral with no residual ownership at all

failure_modes: treating all programs as interchangeable rate sheets differing only in split
taking on registered-ISO overhead and registration duties before volume remotely justifies them
acceptance_tests: each candidate route is written up with who owns the merchant, whose name the seller sells in, who bears liability, and the economics mechanism
revisit_triggers: a candidate program's structure does not match any mapped route
the operator's volume approaches the point where direct registration becomes plausible

nodes.definition: Read a candidate agent agreement for what it actually governs before signing, extracting the clauses that decide whether the agent ever owns anything: residual payment terms and the events that stop payment (termination, minimum-production lapse, broad 'for cause' definitions); survivability of residuals after the agreement ends; portability, assignment and sale rights over the merchant accounts; non-solicit and non-compete scope during and after the term; exclusivity; liability the agent assumes for merchant losses and chargebacks; deconversion and portfolio-transfer mechanics; and who the merchant contractually belongs to. The operating rule is that the agreement, not the recruiter's pitch, defines the deal - every promised economic must be found in the signed text or treated as absent - and professional legal review of the flagged clauses is recommended for the obligation classes involved, not replaced by this operator-level reading.

included: clause extraction across ownership, survivability, portability, non-solicit, quotas, liability, termination
excluded: rendering legal advice on the clauses
residual payment mechanics themselves (sibling KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an amendment, a paid-residual dispute, or a peer agent's termination outcome shows a clause behaving differently than the extraction assumed

pros.claim: Extraction converts recruiter promises into verifiable text before money depends on them
pros.example: a 'lifetime residuals' pitch shown by the signed text to terminate on any minimum-production lapse

cons.claim: Heavy diligence slows signing and can cost the window on a genuinely good program
cons.example: a strong regional ISO closing its recruiting cohort while redlines go back and forth for weeks

failure_modes: signing on the advertised split without reading the termination and survivability events
assuming the book is sellable when assignment requires the ISO's sole-discretion consent
acceptance_tests: a clause-extraction sheet exists per candidate agreement covering residual survivability, portability and assignment, non-solicit scope, production quotas, liability, and termination events, each quoted or explicitly marked absent
revisit_triggers: the program amends its agreement or Schedule A
a residual-payment dispute exposes a clause reading as wrong

nodes.definition: Understand the processing cost stack as a set of mechanisms rather than memorized numbers: interchange is set by the card networks and paid to the issuing bank, varying by card product, merchant category and entry mode; network assessments are set by the networks themselves; the processor adds markup structured as one of the pricing models (interchange-plus, tiered, flat-rate); and the agent's economics arrive as a buy-rate spread or revenue share defined in the program's Schedule A. Literacy means being able to say for each layer who sets it, what moves it, where it appears on a merchant statement, and how to verify the agent's own share on a specific deal from the Schedule A and the monthly residual report - never asserting a rate or split as a general fact, because every one of them is program-, network- and merchant-specific.

included: layer-by-layer attribution (who sets it, what moves it, where it shows)
per-deal verification path via Schedule A and residual report
excluded: asserting any rate, assessment or split as a figure
residual stream computation and payout mechanics (sibling KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: network fee-structure updates or a Schedule A change invalidate the current mechanism map

pros.claim: Mechanism literacy lets the agent explain a statement credibly without inventing numbers
pros.example: explaining to a salon owner why a rewards card costs more to accept than a plain debit card by pointing at the interchange mechanism, not a made-up rate

cons.claim: Mechanism talk can overwhelm an owner who just wants a monthly figure
cons.example: a c-store owner tuning out mid-explanation of entry-mode downgrades and asking 'so what do I pay'

failure_modes: quoting remembered interchange or split numbers as facts that are wrong for this program or merchant
being unable to reconcile the agent's own residual report against the Schedule A
acceptance_tests: for each cost layer the operator can name who sets it, what moves it, where it appears on a statement, and the per-deal verification path; no training artifact states a rate or split as a general fact
revisit_triggers: the networks publish revised interchange or assessment structures
the program restructures its Schedule A mechanics

nodes.definition: Choose one or two beachhead verticals from the local-SMB set (restaurants and food service, salons and personal care, convenience stores, auto repair) using explicit criteria: card-acceptance intensity and ticket profile of the vertical; POS pain intensity, meaning how much the incumbent tooling hurts daily operations; decision-maker accessibility, favoring owner-on-premises trades; density of targets in the trade area; competitive saturation by mega-ISO telesales and vertical ISVs; referral connectivity, because owners inside a vertical talk to each other; and underwriting acceptability of the vertical under the chosen program. The output is a scored, defensible choice - and the score is a heuristic prior to be revised by pipeline evidence, not a market fact.

included: scoring criteria and the beachhead decision
excluded: per-vertical pain detail (its own node)
POS hardware matching to the vertical (sibling KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: stage-conversion and win-rate evidence from the pipeline confirms or contradicts the scorecard

pros.claim: Focus compounds vertical fluency, referrals and a reusable bundle configuration
pros.example: after ten restaurant installs the agent talks tip pooling and kitchen routing natively and gets introduced across the street

cons.claim: A narrow beachhead caps early pipeline and can simply be the wrong pick
cons.example: committing to salons in a trade area where a booking-software ISV already owns the vertical's payment relationships

failure_modes: selling to whoever answers instead of any deliberate vertical, so no fluency or referral loop ever forms
choosing a vertical the program's underwriting routinely declines
acceptance_tests: a vertical scorecard exists with the named criteria scored per candidate vertical and an underwriting-acceptability note per pick
revisit_triggers: pipeline evidence contradicts the scorecard over a full cycle
a competitor saturates the chosen vertical or a new vertical opens in the trade area

nodes.definition: Select the specific ISO or processor program(s) to sign with by fit, after agreement diligence and vertical choice: does the program support the POS lines the target verticals need; does its underwriting appetite cover those verticals, since some programs decline or restrict categories the trade area is full of; what is its reputation among working agents for residual-report accuracy and support responsiveness; how painful is deconversion if the relationship ends; and does the operator need a second program as a fallback for merchants the primary declines or serves badly. Fit is judged against the verticals and the agreement rating together - a rich Schedule A on a program that cannot board or serve the target vertical is worthless, and an ownership-hostile agreement disqualifies a program no matter how good the fit.

included: fit criteria (POS support, underwriting appetite, reputation, deconversion friction)
joint judgment with the agreement rating
excluded: executing underwriting submissions (sibling KB)
asserting any program's split as a figure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: program behavior in production (boarding outcomes, residual accuracy, support quality) diverges from the fit memo

pros.claim: A fallback program keeps deals alive when the primary declines a category or merchant
pros.example: routing a tobacco-adjacent c-store the primary program restricts to a second program that lawfully boards it

cons.claim: Splitting volume across programs weakens the operator's standing and attention in both
cons.example: neither program's channel manager treating the agent as a priority because volume is halved

failure_modes: choosing by headline split while the program cannot support the vertical's POS needs
having no fallback and losing every merchant the primary program declines
acceptance_tests: a signed-program fit memo records POS-line support, underwriting appetite for each target vertical, reputation checks with working agents, and the fallback decision
revisit_triggers: the program changes its supported POS lines or underwriting appetite
residual-report discrepancies or support failures accumulate

nodes.definition: Build, per chosen vertical, the operating-pain profile the sale will ride on, phrased in the merchant's own operational language: restaurants struggle with tip adjustment and pooling, tab management, kitchen routing, online-order aggregation and rush-hour throughput; salons with appointment booking, no-shows, card-on-file consent and commission splits between chairs; convenience stores with age-restricted SKUs, lottery and EBT handling, shrink and multi-register speed; auto repair with estimates that become invoices, card-on-file authorization for completed work, and large-ticket authorization holds. The profile maps each pain to the bundle element that addresses it and honestly marks the pains the agent's stack cannot fix, so the pitch diagnoses in trade language instead of reciting features.

included: per-vertical pain inventories in trade language
excluded: matching a specific POS model to the vertical (sibling KB)
menu or catalog build detail (sibling KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: discovery audits repeatedly surface pains missing from, or contradicting, the current profile

pros.claim: Speaking the vertical's operating language converts a vendor visit into a peer conversation
pros.example: opening with a mechanic about authorization holds on big invoices instead of about rates earns a real audit invitation

cons.claim: A canned pain profile misfires on merchants who deviate from the vertical stereotype
cons.example: a counter-service cafe with no tabs or kitchen routing being pitched full-service restaurant pains

failure_modes: reciting POS features where the merchant wanted their named problem acknowledged
promising a fix for a pain the profile itself marks unfixable by the stack
acceptance_tests: each chosen vertical has a written pain profile in trade language with every pain mapped to a bundle element or explicitly marked out of the stack's reach
revisit_triggers: audits keep surfacing pains the profile lacks
a bundle change alters which pains are addressable

nodes.definition: Enumerate the actual targets: a named-account map of the trade area listing every merchant in the chosen verticals, seeded from drive-bys, walk-ins as a paying customer, local directories and the operator's own knowledge of the area. Per account, record what is observable without pretext: the POS and acceptance stack visible at the counter, the apparent age of the hardware, whether a competitor's decal is on the door, and the trigger events that open deals - a new opening, an ownership change, a 'coming soon' build-out, visible frustration at the register, or a posted card-minimum sign hinting at cost pain. The map is the pipeline's raw material; it turns prospecting from cold spraying into sequenced visits with a reason to walk in.

excluded: pretexting or covert information gathering
any purchase of private data about owners

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: field visits contradict the map's stack observations or trigger events at a noticeable rate

pros.claim: Trigger events convert the map from a static list into timed openings
pros.example: a build-out permit notice putting a soon-to-open taqueria on the visit list weeks before any competitor calls it

cons.claim: Mapping consumes selling hours and decays as the strip turns over
cons.example: a quarter of the c-store entries stale within months as counters change hands unannounced

failure_modes: prospecting without a map and burning visits on closed doors and wrong verticals
recording gossip about owners instead of observable stack facts
acceptance_tests: the map lists named accounts per vertical with observed stack, hardware-age note, competitor presence and any live trigger event, each dated
revisit_triggers: visit outcomes show map entries are stale
a new vertical is added to the beachhead

nodes.definition: Sell disclosure-first as a hard constraint, not a style: before any signature the merchant hears, in plain language, the contract term and what ends it, early-termination mechanics, the total life cost of a hardware lease versus buying the same hardware, who the processor actually is, that underwriting approval is the processor's decision and never guaranteed, and which parts of the bundle come from which provider. No fear-selling: PCI fines, invented 'compliance deadlines' and chargeback horror stories are never used to stampede a signature. Vulnerable-owner care is explicit: with elderly owners, owners reading contracts in a second language, or any owner visibly deferring, the agent slows down, invites the bookkeeper or a family member, leaves documents for review, and treats 'just tell me where to sign' as a stop signal rather than a gift.

excluded: the claim-class register (its own node)
contract drafting or legal advice

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: complaints, cancellations or referral patterns reveal the disclosure set is incomplete or is being skipped under pressure

pros.claim: Disclosure-first selling compounds into the referral flow no ad spend buys in a small trade area
pros.example: a barber who was told plainly what the lease totals were sending three shop owners over within the year

cons.claim: Full disclosure hands hesitant merchants reasons to stall that a pressure close would have rolled past
cons.example: an owner postponing indefinitely after hearing the honest early-termination mechanics of the new agreement

failure_modes: using PCI-fine scare framing to force a same-day signature
letting a deferential owner sign a lease whose total cost was never spoken aloud
acceptance_tests: a written disclosure checklist (term, exit mechanics, lease totals versus purchase, processor identity, underwriting non-guarantee, provider map) is completed and acknowledged before signature on every deal
no script or marketing artifact uses fear framing
revisit_triggers: a merchant complaint or cancellation cites something they were not told
a new bundle element adds a provider the disclosure map does not yet cover

nodes.definition: Maintain a register of the compliance-sensitive claim classes the agent's marketing and scripts touch, each with an approved form and a verify-current-rules flag: use of card-network marks and the naming rules governing how a sub-agent may present itself, since selling in the registered ISO's name versus the agent's own is governed by the program and network registration rules; surcharging and cash-discount program claims, governed by network rules and state or provincial law that differ by jurisdiction - flagged as a class to check currently, never asserted from memory; PCI-related statements, where 'we make you PCI compliant' overstates what any vendor can promise; and general truth-in-advertising obligations on comparisons and testimonials. The register names each obligation class and where to verify it today; it deliberately never encodes rule text, because network rules and statutes change under it.

included: the claim-class register with approved forms
excluded: asserting current rule text as fact
savings-figure rules (its own node)
PCI scoping work at deployment (sibling KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a network rule change, a regulator action in the trade press, or a program compliance notice touches any registered claim class

pros.claim: A register makes compliance checkable at the artifact level instead of living in one person's memory
pros.example: a new flyer audited line-by-line against the register before printing, catching an unregistered trade-name use

cons.claim: A register is only as current as its last verification pass and can lend false confidence
cons.example: a cash-discount script kept in use after a network updated its program rules, because the flag was never re-checked

failure_modes: marketing under a name the program's registration does not permit
pitching a surcharging program from memory in a jurisdiction that restricts it
acceptance_tests: every claim class in live use appears in the register with an approved wording, a jurisdiction/network verification note with date, and its prohibited forms listed beside compliant substitutes
revisit_triggers: a card network updates marketing, surcharge or registration rules
a new claim class enters the scripts (e.g. a new bundle element's marketing)

nodes.definition: Run prospecting through channels ranked for a trust sale in a small trade area: repeated walk-ins as a genuine paying customer who then talks shop; referrals from installed merchants, formalized by asking at moments of delivered value; accountants, bookkeepers and restaurant-supply reps as multipliers who already hold the merchant's financial trust; chamber, merchant-association and vertical-association presence; and only then outbound calling worked against the named-account map. The channel logic is that displacing an incumbent payment relationship requires borrowed or earned trust, which cold volume does not create - a merchant hands three months of statements to someone vouched for, not to a voice on the phone. Scripts exist for every channel, and every claim in them comes from the compliance register.

included: channel ranking and the trust logic behind it
excluded: claims not drawn from the register
post-sale cross-sell into the installed base (sibling KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: signed-merchant attribution shows which channels actually produce the book

pros.claim: Multiplier channels deliver pre-trusted introductions that unlock statement collection fast
pros.example: a bookkeeper introducing the agent to four restaurant clients whose statements arrive at the first meeting

cons.claim: Trust channels ramp slowly and depend on a small number of relationships
cons.example: months of chamber breakfasts before the first introduction, while a telesales competitor blankets the same strip in a week

failure_modes: leading with cold calls and training the trade area to see the agent as another rate peddler
burning a multiplier's trust with one oversold deal
acceptance_tests: a channel plan exists ranking channels with the trust rationale, referral-ask moments are defined, and all scripts trace their claims to the register
revisit_triggers: channel-level pipeline data contradicts the ranking
a key multiplier relationship ends or sours

nodes.definition: Design the bundle that makes the agent one accountable relationship instead of a rate quote: POS plus card acceptance is the anchor; candidate elements are business phone/VoIP, primary or backup internet, cameras and basic security, and a support plan under which the merchant calls one number for all of it. The architecture decisions: which elements anchor stickiness (the POS and the support habit) versus which mainly add margin; which the agent can source, install and support in this trade area at real quality; and sequencing - lead with the anchor, attach elements at need moments rather than forcing the full stack on day one. The explicit rule: an element the agent cannot support locally stays out of the bundle, because a failed camera install poisons the processing relationship that actually pays.

excluded: installing or servicing the elements (sibling KB)
cross-sell into already-installed merchants (sibling KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: service-ticket volume, attach rates or vendor changes show an element's role or serviceability was misjudged

pros.claim: A multi-element relationship raises switching cost far beyond what a rate quote can defend
pros.example: a competitor's lower headline pitch failing because the agent also runs the c-store's phones, internet backup and cameras

cons.claim: Every added element adds a failure surface the agent answers for personally
cons.example: a flaky VoIP vendor turning the agent's phone into the complaint line for dropped orders

failure_modes: bundling an element with no local service capability behind it
forcing the full stack on day one and losing the anchor sale to complexity
acceptance_tests: the bundle design names each element's role (anchor, stickiness, margin), its sourcing and local service path, and its attach moment; undeliverable elements are excluded in writing
revisit_triggers: an element's vendor or service quality changes
attach-rate and service-ticket experience contradicts an element's assumed role

nodes.definition: Structure the first real meeting as a diagnostic walkthrough, not a pitch: walk the merchant's operation and record the POS make, age and its pain points at the counter; the phone and internet bills and their contract status; camera coverage gaps; how cards are accepted today and where lines back up; then ask for the processing statements - the most recent three months, full pages, not the summary sheet - and the current processing and hardware contracts. The audit openly states why the documents are needed: to diagnose rather than promise. Its output is the merchant-specific fact base every later step consumes - the statement diagnostic, the bundle configuration, the proposal, the risk screen - and a merchant who declines to share documents is a signal to slow down, not to pitch harder.

included: the walkthrough checklist (POS, phones, internet, cameras, acceptance flow)
full multi-month statement and contract collection
excluded: the statement diagnostic itself (its own node)
site survey for installation purposes (sibling KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: downstream steps repeatedly lack facts the walkthrough was supposed to capture

pros.claim: A documented walkthrough surfaces bundle openings no statement shows
pros.example: noticing the salon's dead camera at the register and a month-to-month internet bill during one visit

cons.claim: A thorough audit asks busy owners for time and paperwork before any visible payoff
cons.example: a mechanic postponing twice because pulling statements means an evening in the back office

failure_modes: pitching from the doorway and never earning the documents
accepting the summary page and treating it as an audit
acceptance_tests: each audited merchant has a walkthrough record plus collected full statements and contracts, or a dated note of what is missing and why the diagnostic is deferred
revisit_triggers: proposals keep failing on facts the walkthrough should have caught
the bundle changes and the walkthrough checklist must widen

nodes.definition: Read the merchant's processing statements as a diagnostic mechanism: identify the pricing model in force (tiered, flat-rate, interchange-plus, or a bundled hybrid) from the statement's own structure; compute the effective rate - total fees over total volume for the period - as a descriptive ratio of that merchant's actual mix; locate what drives it (card mix, downgrade patterns from entry mode or settlement timing, ancillary and junk fees, monthly minimums, equipment and gateway charges); and separate what a new setup could structurally change from what it cannot, since interchange itself moves only if the merchant's mix or acceptance behavior moves. The output is a written diagnostic of this merchant's statements - never a generic rate comparison and never a savings promise - and multiple months are required because any single month can misstate seasonal mix.

included: effective-rate computation from the merchant's own numbers
excluded: savings promises or guaranteed comparisons
repricing execution after conversion (sibling KBs)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: post-conversion statements confirm or contradict the diagnostic's driver attributions

pros.claim: A driver-level diagnostic earns credibility no rate pitch can, because the merchant sees their own numbers explained
pros.example: showing a restaurant owner the keyed-entry downgrades their staff causes on phone orders, line by line on their own statement

cons.claim: Statement formats are inconsistent and some deliberately obscure the fee structure
cons.example: a bundled statement that shows no interchange detail at all, capping what any honest diagnostic can conclude

failure_modes: reading a tiered statement as interchange-plus and diagnosing drivers that are not there
extrapolating a single month across a seasonal year
acceptance_tests: each diagnostic names the pricing model, shows the effective-rate computation from the merchant's own statement, itemizes fee drivers, and marks structurally changeable versus unchangeable components
diagnostics built from partial statements are labeled as bounded by the missing pages or months
revisit_triggers: post-conversion verification contradicts a diagnostic's driver attribution
a processor reformats statements in a way that breaks the reading method

nodes.definition: Govern every savings statement the agent makes: the claim form 'we will definitely save you X percent' - or any guaranteed figure, before or after analysis - is prohibited. A savings figure may be uttered only as a conditional estimate derived from the merchant's own analyzed statements, stated with its assumptions (same volume, same card mix, the proposed pricing model and fee schedule) and with a commitment that it will be verified against real post-conversion statements, with the agent owning that follow-up. When analysis shows little to save because the merchant is already near structural cost, the discipline requires saying so and repositioning on service and bundle value or walking away; manufacturing a savings story to rescue a pitch is precisely the failure this node exists to prevent.

included: the conditional-estimate format with stated assumptions
excluded: the diagnostic computation itself (its own node)
executing the verification on later residual data (sibling KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: post-conversion verifications and any complaint or regulator signal test whether the discipline is holding in the field

pros.claim: Conditional, verified estimates survive the merchant's accountant and the post-conversion reality check
pros.example: an estimate labeled 'at your current volume and card mix' holding up at the ninety-day verification and producing a referral

cons.claim: Conditional language sounds weaker at the table than a competitor's illegitimate guarantee
cons.example: losing a c-store to a telesales rep who promised a definite number no one will ever audit

failure_modes: converting a diagnostic into a guaranteed number under closing pressure
quietly skipping the post-conversion verification the estimate promised
acceptance_tests: no script, ad, proposal or recorded pitch carries an unconditional savings figure
every written estimate carries its assumptions and a named post-conversion verification step
low-savings findings are disclosed to the merchant as such
revisit_triggers: a verification shows estimates running systematically hot or cold
advertising-rule or network guidance touching savings claims changes

nodes.definition: Assemble the proposal from the audit and the diagnostic: the bundle configuration mapped to the merchant's named pains; the recommended pricing model with a mechanism explanation the owner can repeat (what interchange is, what the markup is, why this model fits their mix); the hardware path - purchase, lease, or placement/rental - with the total cost of each over the commitment period shown side by side; any conditional savings estimate in the discipline's format; the support promise in service terms the agent controls (who answers, response expectations); and the term, exit and provider disclosures the disclosure ethic requires. One page the owner understands beats ten pages of rate tables - the proposal is written to be re-read by the owner's accountant without the agent in the room and still hold up.

excluded: hardware model selection detail (sibling KB)
any figure not derived from this merchant's documents

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: close rates and accountant-stage outcomes show whether the proposal format is doing its job

pros.claim: A proposal that survives the accountant's unattended read closes slower but sticks
pros.example: a restaurant's bookkeeper approving the one-page proposal because every number traced to the statements she already knew

cons.claim: Side-by-side lease-versus-purchase totals can kill the agent's richest hardware structure
cons.example: an owner choosing outright purchase once the lease's life total sits next to it in print

failure_modes: hiding the lease total behind a monthly figure
proposing bundle elements never verified deliverable at this site
acceptance_tests: every proposal shows hardware path totals side by side, ties each bundle element to a named pain, embeds the disclosure set, and formats any savings figure per the discipline
revisit_triggers: proposals die at the accountant stage for a recurring reason
the bundle or program changes what can be proposed

nodes.definition: Position against the four competitor classes a local agent actually meets: mega-ISO telesales selling teaser structures that decay after boarding; banks bundling processing into the deposit relationship and winning on inertia; self-serve ISV and payfac stacks (Square- and Toast-class) that win on onboarding ease and software fit but leave no local human accountable; and the rival local agent selling the same wedge. The honest wedge is the bundle relationship - one local operator accountable for POS, acceptance, phones, internet and cameras, with same-day physical presence - argued by contrasting service models and relationship structure, never by inventing competitor pricing or making unverifiable claims about a named rival. Against the self-serve stacks the position concedes their genuine strengths and targets merchants whose complexity or service need exceeds what self-serve delivers.

included: the four competitor classes and the wedge per class
excluded: deceptive comparison or rival-badmouthing
matching competitor claim forms the compliance register prohibits

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: lost-deal attributions by competitor class show which wedges land and which fail

pros.claim: Conceding a competitor's real strengths makes the wedge credible where blanket superiority talk fails
pros.example: telling a food truck that a self-serve stack genuinely fits them, and being remembered when their sit-down location opens

cons.claim: A service-and-relationship wedge is hard to prove before the merchant has experienced it
cons.example: same-day-presence promises sounding like every rep's talk until the first real outage proves them

failure_modes: arguing price against a teaser structure and losing on a number no one will honor
badmouthing a named rival with claims the merchant can check and find false
acceptance_tests: a positioning sheet exists per competitor class with the wedge, the conceded strengths, and the prohibited argument forms
revisit_triggers: lost-deal notes show a competitor class winning for an unmodeled reason
a new competitor class enters the trade area

nodes.definition: Manage the switch away from an incumbent processor or POS: surface the real switching costs before asking for a signature - the processing contract's remaining term and early-termination fee, a hardware lease that survives the switch and keeps billing, gift-card balances and data locked in the old POS, and staff retraining time - read from the merchant's own documents, which the merchant reads and confirms; the agent never advises breaching a contract and never estimates an ETF by guessing. The displacement decision is then the merchant's arithmetic, framed conditionally: confirmed switching cost against diagnosed benefit, sometimes concluding 'wait for your term to end' - an honest wait that often wins the deal later plus a referral now. Urgency manufactured against the merchant's contract reality is fear-selling and prohibited.

excluded: advising contract breach or interpreting contract law
guessing ETF or lease figures on the merchant's behalf

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: conversion experiences reveal switching costs the displacement checklist does not yet surface

pros.claim: Merchant-confirmed switching math prevents the broken-promise blowup at conversion
pros.example: the surviving equipment lease discovered and priced into the decision before signing, not on the first double-billed month

cons.claim: Honest switching math delays or kills deals a pressure close would capture
cons.example: a salon deferring nine months to its contract end after seeing its own ETF in writing

failure_modes: waving away an ETF the merchant later pays angrily
manufacturing urgency against a contract the merchant has not re-read
acceptance_tests: every displacement file shows term, ETF and lease facts confirmed by the merchant from their own documents before switch math was presented
revisit_triggers: a conversion surfaces a switching cost the process missed
incumbent contract structures in the trade area change shape

nodes.definition: Screen every prospective merchant for fit before proposal and submission, on the agent's own account: category acceptability under the chosen program, since each program prohibits or restricts categories (CBD, vape, firearms-adjacent, aggregation-prone models among them) and boarding an unacceptable category wastes the deal and burns program credibility; red flags visible pre-underwriting (a trail of prior processor terminations, chargeback stories told proudly, requests to run someone else's sales through the account); expectation fit, declining merchants who will sign only for guarantees the discipline prohibits; and service fit, where the operation is one the bundle cannot actually serve. The screen yields sign, decline, or refer-elsewhere - while underwriting itself remains the processor's decision and is never promised: the screen filters what the agent submits, it does not predict approval.

included: category check against the current program lists
excluded: the underwriting decision itself (the processor's)
KYC document mechanics (sibling KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: underwriting kill-rates on submitted deals and program list revisions test the screen's calibration

pros.claim: Screening before proposing saves the whole downstream chain from deals that cannot survive
pros.example: catching a smoke shop's CBD shelf at the audit stage instead of after the application bounces

cons.claim: A conservative screen turns away oddball merchants who would have boarded fine
cons.example: declining an unusual hybrid retail concept the processor would actually have approved

failure_modes: submitting a category the program prohibits and burning credibility with the channel manager
promising a nervous merchant they will be approved
acceptance_tests: every submitted deal carries a completed screen record (category check against the current program list, red-flag notes, expectation check)
declined merchants receive an honest reason and no deal file contains an approval promise
revisit_triggers: underwriting outcomes diverge from screen predictions in either direction
the program revises its prohibited or restricted category lists

nodes.definition: Run the close as expectation-setting: the merchant signs an application to the processor, not a guarantee of approval, and the agent says exactly that; the timeline is stated as stages (underwriting review, approval or stipulations, hardware arrival, install, go-live) with ownership named for each; every promise made during the sale - pricing model and fee schedule, bundle contents, support commitments, the conditional savings estimate and its verification step - is written into a recap the merchant keeps; and the disclosure checklist is confirmed complete before any signature. The close also books the deployment conversation on the spot rather than leaving go-live vague, because the gap between signature and a working counter is where sold deals die - and where the deployment sibling KB takes over.

excluded: running underwriting or chasing stipulations (sibling KB)
install scheduling mechanics (sibling KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cancellation timing and deployment feedback show whether closes are setting durable expectations

pros.claim: A written promises recap prevents the sales-versus-deployment contradiction that kills trust at go-live
pros.example: the installer reading the recap and configuring exactly the tip flow the owner was promised at the table

cons.claim: Explicit underwriting caveats can spook a merchant at the emotional peak of the close
cons.example: an owner hesitating after hearing approval is the processor's call, where a competitor said 'you're all set'

failure_modes: letting the merchant believe signature equals approval
closing with promises that exist only in the conversation's memory
acceptance_tests: every closed deal has a signed application, a written promises recap in the merchant's hands, an underwriting non-guarantee acknowledgment, and a booked deployment next step
revisit_triggers: post-signature cancellations cluster in the signature-to-go-live gap
deployment reports promises missing from recaps

nodes.definition: Package the sold deal into the artifact the deployment-and-onboarding process consumes, and end acquisition's job there: the package carries the application data as submitted; the exact bundle scope sold, element by element with providers; the written promises recap verbatim; the statement baseline - the analyzed statements and the diagnostic - so post-conversion savings verification has its reference point; the vertical pain profile and site facts from the audit (counter layout, connectivity findings, camera locations); and the open risks the screen flagged. A complete package prevents the classic failure of deployment re-discovering the merchant from scratch and contradicting what sales promised, and the boundary is explicit: hardware matching, underwriting chasing, installation, menu build and training belong downstream in the sibling KB's territory.

included: the statement baseline for later verification
excluded: performing any deployment step
post-go-live account management (sibling KBs)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: deployment rework attributable to package gaps rises or falls after a contract change

pros.claim: A contracted package makes the acquisition-to-deployment seam auditable instead of tribal
pros.example: a returned package rejected for a missing statement baseline before the install was ever scheduled

cons.claim: Package assembly is unpaid admin at the exact moment the seller wants the next deal
cons.example: recap and baseline files landing half-complete on a Friday because two new audits were booked

failure_modes: handing off a deal as a name and a phone number
omitting the statement baseline and making the savings estimate permanently unverifiable
acceptance_tests: every handoff package contains application data, element-by-element bundle scope with providers, the verbatim promises recap, the statement baseline, site facts, and flagged risks - or is rejected back
revisit_triggers: deployment reports missing or contradictory package contents
the downstream intake contract changes

nodes.definition: Run acquisition as a measured pipeline with explicit stages - mapped, first-contacted, audit done, statements collected, diagnostic delivered, proposed, signed, submitted, handed off - and a working cadence over the named-account map: visit blocks, follow-up clocks per stage, referral asks after delivered value. Metrics are mechanisms, not quotas pulled from air: stage-to-stage conversion identifies where deals die (statements never collected points at trust or audit problems; proposals dying unanswered points at diagnostic or pricing-story problems), and channel-level attribution shows where signed merchants actually come from. These readings are heuristic priors until enough deals accumulate, and they exist to feed the revision loops - vertical choice, channel ranking, bundle design - not to decorate a dashboard.

included: stage-conversion and channel attribution as diagnostic mechanisms
excluded: book-level retention and portfolio metrics (sibling KB)
inventing benchmark conversion numbers as targets

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: accumulated deal volume turns the heuristic stage and channel readings into observed patterns

pros.claim: Stage-conversion readings localize the pipeline's actual failure point instead of prompting generic 'sell harder'
pros.example: seeing audits complete but statements never arrive, which indicts the document ask, not the prospecting

cons.claim: Small-volume pipelines produce noisy readings that invite overcorrection
cons.example: abandoning a channel after a handful of losses that were really seasonal timing

failure_modes: treating early noisy conversion readings as truths and thrashing the strategy
tracking activity volume while never recording why deals died
acceptance_tests: the pipeline has named stages, every account on the map carries a stage and a dated next action, and lost deals carry a recorded reason
revisit_triggers: a stage's conversion shifts materially and persistently
channel attribution contradicts the current channel ranking

edges.why_related: the route-to-market map is read against what the operator wants the book to be, not against recruiter pitches
clause extraction presumes knowing which route's agreement is being read and what that structure can even govern
which economics mechanisms apply (buy-rate spread, revenue share, referral fee) depends on the route chosen
the vertical scoring criteria are derived from the book-first thesis rather than raw deal availability
a program is only selectable after its agreement's ownership and termination clauses are extracted and rated
comparing candidate programs' Schedule A mechanics requires the layer-by-layer mechanism map
pain profiles are built only for the verticals the beachhead decision selected
the account map enumerates the trade area's merchants in the chosen verticals
bundle elements are chosen for the pains the profile names, not assembled from what vendors offer
the channels are worked against the named-account map's sequenced visits and trigger events
the audit invitation - and the statements it collects - is earned through the trust channels
the full multi-month statements and contracts the diagnostic reads are collected by the audit
reading a statement requires knowing who sets each layer and where it appears on the page
a conditional estimate can only be derived from a completed merchant-specific diagnostic
the naming and registration claim rules depend on the route: whose name the agent is permitted to sell in
the proposal's pricing recommendation and any estimate are assembled from the diagnostic
the proposal configures the designed bundle for this merchant's named pains
the screen's category acceptability check reads the chosen program's current prohibited and restricted lists
the close recaps and papers exactly what the disclosed proposal offered
the package carries forward the application, recap and booked next step the close produced
displacement arithmetic is argued against a concrete disclosed proposal, not an abstract offer
the proposal must carry the term, exit, lease-total and provider disclosures in owner-readable form
no signature is taken until the disclosure checklist is complete and acknowledged
outreach materials and scripts may use only register-approved claims and the permitted selling identity
any savings figure in a proposal must be conditional, assumption-labeled and derived from this merchant's statements
differentiation may not cross into deceptive comparison or unverifiable claims about named rivals
displacement urgency rewards exactly the guaranteed-savings talk the discipline prohibits
edges.resolution_rule: the claim discipline wins unconditionally: displacement waits for a statement-grounded conditional estimate, and a deal that only closes on a guarantee is not taken

edges.why_related: pipeline pressure to hit signing cadence pushes against declining bad-fit merchants
edges.resolution_rule: the screen wins; a thin pipeline is fixed upstream with more mapping and prospecting, never by admitting merchants the screen rejects

edges.why_related: lease-heavy hardware structures maximize upfront margin exactly where total-cost disclosure deters signing
edges.resolution_rule: disclosure wins: lease totals are shown side by side with purchase, and a deal that survives only undisclosed is declined

edges.why_related: the program with the best vertical and POS fit can carry the worst residual-ownership terms
edges.resolution_rule: book-ownership terms dominate headline fit and split; fit gaps are covered with a second program rather than accepting ownership-hostile paper

edges.why_related: the vertical's dominant pains drive which wedge - service depth or software fit - actually lands
disclosure-first treatment of early merchants generates the referral flow the trust channels depend on
screen quality determines how many handed-off deals survive underwriting and deploy cleanly
diagnose-then-propose is a fixed order: no proposal before the walkthrough and statement collection are done
pipeline stages are seeded from the named-account map before cadence measurement means anything
stage-conversion and win-rate evidence revises the vertical scorecard's heuristic priors
channel-level signed-merchant attribution re-ranks the prospecting channels
deployment reports of missing facts or contradicted promises tighten what the close must capture
both govern permissible speech: one is the savings-specific rule set, the other the register of all compliance-sensitive claim classes

conflict_axes.name: richest_split_vs_book_ownership
conflict_axes.description: Programs advertising the richest revenue share often carry the weakest residual-survivability and portability terms, so the headline economics and the durable asset pull in opposite directions.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: rate agreements on ownership clauses first and treat the split as a tiebreaker among ownership-acceptable programs

conflict_axes.name: closing_power_vs_claim_compliance
conflict_axes.description: The most persuasive claim forms - guaranteed savings, scare framing, unverifiable comparisons - are exactly the prohibited ones, so pitch strength and compliance trade off at the table.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: compliance wins every instance; the compensating strength is the diagnostic's credibility, not a stronger claim

conflict_axes.name: bundle_breadth_vs_serviceability
conflict_axes.description: Each added bundle element deepens stickiness and margin but adds a failure surface the agent must personally answer for in a small trade area.
poles: sell only what is locally serviceable
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: cap the bundle at proven local service capability and add elements only with a vetted service path

conflict_axes.name: speed_to_close_vs_disclosure_depth
conflict_axes.description: Completing the full disclosure set slows the close and gives hesitant merchants exits, while skipping it closes faster and plants the churn and complaint seeds.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: disclosure is non-negotiable; manage speed by preparing disclosure materials before the closing meeting

conflict_axes.name: upfront_hardware_margin_vs_relationship_trust
conflict_axes.description: Lease-heavy hardware structures pay the agent most today and breed the resentment that costs the residual relationship tomorrow.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: show lease and purchase totals side by side and let the disclosed choice be the merchant's; book economics favor durability

conflict_axes.name: beachhead_focus_vs_opportunistic_volume
conflict_axes.description: Vertical focus compounds fluency and referrals but says no to reachable off-vertical deals that would pay this month.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: take off-vertical deals only when they cost no beachhead capacity and never reshape the bundle around them

conflict_axes.name: displacement_urgency_vs_switching_cost_honesty
conflict_axes.description: The agent wants the switch now, but the merchant's confirmed ETF and surviving lease sometimes make waiting the honest recommendation.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: run the merchant-confirmed arithmetic and accept the wait outcome; the honest wait converts later and refers now

conflict_axes.name: pipeline_volume_vs_merchant_quality
conflict_axes.description: Cadence targets reward signing whoever is available while the screen exists to decline exactly those marginal merchants.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the screen fixed and treat pipeline shortfalls as an upstream mapping and prospecting problem

conflict_axes.name: local_trust_depth_vs_outreach_scale
conflict_axes.description: Walk-ins, referrals and multiplier relationships build the trust a displacement sale needs but scale far slower than blanket outreach.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: lead with trust channels and use cold outreach only against mapped accounts with a live trigger event

edge_cases.description: The merchant hands over only the statement's summary page, hiding the interchange detail and fee pages
edge_cases.trigger: statement collection yields partial pages or a single month
edge_cases.mitigation: request full statements for the most recent three months before any diagnostic; if refused, deliver a diagnostic explicitly labeled as bounded by the missing pages and make no savings estimate from it

edge_cases.description: The prospect runs on a flat-rate self-serve stack and has no conventional processing statement to analyze
edge_cases.trigger: a Square-class payfac merchant enters discovery
edge_cases.mitigation: diagnose from the stack's own reporting exports and the merchant's card-mix reality; compare relationship structures honestly and concede where self-serve genuinely fits

edge_cases.description: The merchant demands 'guarantee you will beat my rate or no deal'
edge_cases.trigger: a prospect conditions signing on a guaranteed savings figure
edge_cases.mitigation: explain the conditional-estimate-plus-verification mechanism; if the merchant will only sign on a guarantee, decline the deal - the prohibited claim is not available as a closing tool

edge_cases.description: A non-cancellable POS hardware lease survives the processor switch and keeps billing the merchant
edge_cases.trigger: discovery finds a third-party equipment lease independent of the processing contract
edge_cases.mitigation: surface the lease's remaining obligation from the merchant's own documents before proposing; include it in the switching-cost arithmetic and never imply the new deal erases it

edge_cases.description: An attractive local merchant falls in a category the chosen program prohibits or restricts
edge_cases.trigger: category screening hits the program's prohibited or restricted list, such as CBD retail inside the c-store vertical
edge_cases.mitigation: check the current program category list before proposing; decline or route to a program that lawfully boards the category, and never coach category misdescription on an application

edge_cases.description: A post-termination non-solicit that would strand the book is discovered only after the program is signed
edge_cases.trigger: agreement diligence was skipped or shallow and a dispute surfaces the clause
edge_cases.mitigation: extract termination, survivability and non-solicit clauses before signing; if already signed, obtain professional review of the clause before any move that could trigger it

edge_cases.description: An installed merchant's referral arrives expecting an undisclosed 'friend deal' with side promises
edge_cases.trigger: a referral shows up with pricing expectations set by word of mouth
edge_cases.mitigation: run the standard audit, diagnostic and disclosure path; any accommodation is written into the recap, never left as a verbal side promise

edge_cases.description: An elderly owner, or an owner reading the contract in a second language, is ready to sign without understanding the lease totals
edge_cases.trigger: vulnerable-owner signals appear at the close
edge_cases.mitigation: slow the close: plain-language walkthrough, documents left for review, bookkeeper or family invited; treat a deferential 'just tell me where to sign' as a stop signal

edge_cases.description: A bundle element fails presale - the internet provider cannot serve the address or the camera work exceeds the agent's capability
edge_cases.trigger: a proposed bundle element proves undeliverable at this site
edge_cases.mitigation: verify each element's deliverability before it enters the proposal; drop undeliverable elements openly rather than substituting silently after signature

edge_cases.description: The statement diagnostic shows the merchant is already near structural cost with little to save
edge_cases.trigger: analysis finds a well-priced incumbent deal
edge_cases.mitigation: say so plainly; reposition on service, bundle and local accountability, or advise staying put - the honest no-savings answer builds the referral channel

edge_cases.description: A competitor drops a too-good-to-be-true counter-offer - free hardware and an implausible headline rate - mid-deal
edge_cases.trigger: the merchant brings a competing offer that looks deceptive
edge_cases.mitigation: never match the deceptive form; give the merchant the questions that reveal how such offers recover their cost (rate decay, added fees, lease terms) and let the diagnostic speak

edge_cases.description: A seasonal merchant's single statement month misrepresents the annual card mix and volume
edge_cases.trigger: seasonality is detected or suspected in the vertical, such as an ice-cream counter audited in winter
edge_cases.mitigation: collect months spanning the seasonal cycle or label the estimate as season-bounded and widen its stated assumptions accordingly

workflow.description: State what acquisition exists to produce and the positioning and ethics it commits to
workflow.gate: the charter states the book-of-merchants asset logic, the bundle-relationship positioning, and the ethical-selling commitments

workflow.description: Map every cost-stack layer to who sets it, what moves it, and how it is verified per deal
workflow.gate: each layer carries its setter, its movers, its statement location, and a per-deal verification path, with no rate or split stated as fact

workflow.description: Extract and rate the ownership, survivability, non-solicit, quota, liability and termination clauses per candidate program
workflow.gate: every deciding clause is quoted or marked absent and the agreement is rated before any signature

workflow.description: Score candidate verticals on the explicit criteria and pick one or two beachheads
workflow.gate: the chosen verticals carry scored criteria and an underwriting-acceptability note

workflow.action: Select and sign the program by fit
workflow.description: Match agreement-rated programs to the chosen verticals' POS and underwriting needs, with a fallback decision
workflow.gate: the signed program supports the target verticals and passed the agreement rating; the fallback decision is recorded

workflow.action: Profile vertical pains and design the bundle
workflow.description: Write each vertical's pain profile in trade language and map pains to locally serviceable bundle elements
workflow.gate: every pain maps to a deliverable bundle element or is marked out of the stack's reach; undeliverable elements are excluded in writing

workflow.description: Build the claims register and the savings-claim discipline before any outreach exists
workflow.gate: savings, surcharge/cash-discount, PCI and network-mark claim classes each carry an approved form and a dated verify-current-rules note

workflow.description: Enumerate named accounts per vertical with observed stack facts and trigger events
workflow.gate: accounts are enumerated per vertical with dated stack observations and any live trigger events

workflow.description: Work the ranked channels over the map, with scripts drawn from the register
workflow.gate: outreach uses only register-approved claims and the permitted selling identity

workflow.action: Conduct discovery audits and statement diagnostics
workflow.description: Walk the operation, collect full statements and contracts, and produce the merchant-specific diagnostic
workflow.artifact: per-merchant diagnostic file (walkthrough record plus statement diagnostic)
workflow.gate: the diagnostic rests on full multi-month statements or is labeled bounded, and carries no unconditional savings figure

workflow.action: Propose, screen and close with expectations set
workflow.description: Assemble the disclosed proposal, pass the risk-fit screen, and close on written expectations
workflow.artifact: disclosed proposal, screen record, signed application and promises recap
workflow.gate: the disclosure checklist is acknowledged, the screen record is complete, underwriting is stated as the processor's decision, and the recap is in the merchant's hands

workflow.action: Package the handoff and log the pipeline
workflow.description: Assemble the deployment handoff package and record the deal's pipeline journey
workflow.artifact: deployment handoff package and updated pipeline record
workflow.gate: the package contains application data, bundle scope, promises recap, statement baseline, site facts and flagged risks; the pipeline stage and lost-deal reasons are current

priority_rationale: Program-and-economics foundations (thesis, route map, agreement diligence, mechanism literacy) precede vertical and market targeting because they define what the agent may sell and own; targeting precedes the sales method because the bundle, channels and pain language are vertical-specific; the compliance and disclosure guardrails stand before the first pitch because retracting claims costs more than never making them; and the diagnostic-proposal-close chain ends in a screened, disclosed, packaged handoff so deployment inherits deals that survive underwriting and keep their promises.

dominance_rules.rationale: one deceptive claim can taint the book, the program relationship, and the agent's legal exposure; no single deal is worth it
dominance_rules.trigger: a compliant framing weakens the pitch or a prohibited framing would close the deal
dominance_rules.action: use only the register-approved form and lose the deal rather than the claim discipline

dominance_rules.rule: Book-ownership terms dominate the advertised split
dominance_rules.rationale: a rich split on paper the agent does not own pays only until the program decides otherwise
dominance_rules.trigger: candidate programs differ on residual survivability or portability versus headline economics
dominance_rules.action: choose the ownership-stronger agreement and cover fit gaps with a second program

dominance_rules.rationale: savings are merchant-specific findings to verify, not sales instruments to assert
dominance_rules.trigger: any savings figure is about to be spoken or written
dominance_rules.action: derive it from this merchant's analyzed statements as a conditional estimate or do not utter it

dominance_rules.rationale: an undisclosed term surfacing after signature converts a sale into a churn event and a reputation wound
dominance_rules.trigger: the merchant is ready to sign before the disclosure checklist is complete
dominance_rules.action: complete the checklist first, even at the cost of a second visit

dominance_rules.rule: The processor's underwriting authority dominates any sales promise
dominance_rules.rationale: approval is not the agent's to give; promising it manufactures a broken promise
dominance_rules.trigger: a merchant asks whether they will be approved or a close drifts toward assurance
dominance_rules.action: state that underwriting decides, describe the stages, and promise only what the agent controls

dominance_rules.rule: The merchant risk-fit screen dominates pipeline volume targets
dominance_rules.rationale: a bad-fit merchant costs more in churn, chargebacks and program credibility than an empty pipeline slot
dominance_rules.trigger: cadence metrics are behind and a marginal merchant is available to sign
dominance_rules.action: apply the screen unchanged and fix the pipeline upstream with more mapping and prospecting

dominance_rules.rationale: one failed bundle element poisons the processing relationship that pays the residual
dominance_rules.trigger: an element the agent cannot locally support would fatten a proposal
dominance_rules.action: leave it out, or bring in a vetted local partner who explicitly owns its service

dominance_rules.rule: The merchant's own documents dominate the agent's displacement arithmetic
dominance_rules.rationale: ETF and lease facts guessed wrong become the agent's broken promise at the worst possible moment
dominance_rules.trigger: switching costs are being quantified for a displacement decision
dominance_rules.action: have the merchant read and confirm term, ETF and lease facts from their contracts before any switch math is presented

dominance_rules.rule: Beachhead focus dominates opportunistic one-off deals during the ramp
dominance_rules.rationale: vertical fluency, referrals and a reusable bundle only compound inside a focus
dominance_rules.trigger: an off-vertical deal appears while the beachhead pipeline is unproven
dominance_rules.action: take it only if it costs no beachhead capacity and never reshape the bundle around it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Extract and rate the agreement's ownership clauses before signing any merchant under the program
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building a residual book on paper the agent does not own and re-papering merchants later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build economics mechanism literacy before performing any statement analysis
anti_rework_rules.prevents: misread statements, retracted diagnostics, and trust that must be re-won

anti_rework_rules.rule: Choose beachhead verticals before designing the bundle
anti_rework_rules.prevents: redesigning the bundle merchant by merchant instead of configuring a vertical template

anti_rework_rules.rule: Stand up the compliant-claims register before the first outreach
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recalling marketing, retraining scripts, and repairing claims already loose in the trade area

anti_rework_rules.rule: Collect full multi-month statements before any savings estimate
anti_rework_rules.prevents: estimates built on partial data that must be walked back after conversion

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the risk-fit screen before writing the proposal
anti_rework_rules.prevents: proposals, submissions and merchant expectations spent on deals underwriting will kill

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify each bundle element's deliverability at the site before it enters the proposal
anti_rework_rules.prevents: post-signature substitutions and the broken-promise cleanup they trigger

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the promises recap at the close, not from memory later
anti_rework_rules.prevents: sales-versus-deployment contradictions that must be renegotiated with the merchant

anti_rework_rules.rule: Baseline the analyzed statements in the handoff package
anti_rework_rules.prevents: post-conversion savings verification with no reference point, leaving the estimate permanently unverifiable

iteration_protocol.trigger: post-conversion verification shows a delivered outcome materially off the conditional estimate
iteration_protocol.action: re-examine the diagnostic's assumptions, tighten estimate language, and inform the merchant proactively

iteration_protocol.trigger: the program amends its agreement, Schedule A, or category lists
iteration_protocol.action: re-run clause extraction and economics verification and re-check pending deals against the new category list

iteration_protocol.trigger: a claim-bearing rule changes - network marketing rules, surcharge or cash-discount law, PCI guidance
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the claims register, retrain the scripts, and pull affected marketing from circulation

iteration_protocol.trigger: win rate in a beachhead vertical stays poor across a full pipeline cycle
iteration_protocol.action: revisit the vertical scorecard and pain profile against what the lost-deal notes actually say

iteration_protocol.trigger: a bundle element repeatedly fails presale or in service
iteration_protocol.action: redesign or drop the element and update the vertical bundle template

iteration_protocol.trigger: deployment reports handoff packages missing facts or contradicting sales promises
iteration_protocol.action: extend the package contract and the close recap so the gap cannot recur

iteration_protocol.trigger: submitted deals die in underwriting at an elevated rate
iteration_protocol.action: tighten the screen's category and red-flag checks and reassess processor fit for the vertical

iteration_protocol.trigger: one competitor offer class recurs across lost deals
iteration_protocol.action: update the positioning and displacement handling for that class without adopting its claim forms
